item.title: Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality, Insult, injury, bondage, That one stands firm, Like a mountain unshaken — Such a monk, Pleasure and pain…
item.description:
Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality,
Insult, injury, bondage,
That one stands firm,
Like a mountain unshaken —
Such a monk,
Pleasure and pain do not disturb.

From: Udana 3.3

item.title: “Form, sound, taste, smell, touch — All these things Are desirable, delightful, agreeable As long as they exist. The world with its devas Regards them…
item.description:
“Form, sound, taste, smell, touch —
All these things
Are desirable, delightful, agreeable
As long as they exist.

The world with its devas
Regards them as delightful,
But when they cease,
Then they are seen as suffering.

The noble ones see as happiness
The destruction of identity.
This is completely opposite
To what the whole world sees.

What others call happiness,
The noble call suffering.
What others call suffering,
The noble know as happiness.

The good have open eyes, they see, they have light —
Apart from the noble ones,
Who is worthy of perfect enlightenment?
By that right knowledge of the path,
They attain Nibbāna, free from defilements.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.12
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these four noble searches. What four? Here, monks, a person being himself subject to aging, having known the peril in what is…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these four noble searches. What four? Here, monks, a person being himself subject to aging, having known the peril in what is subject to aging, seeks the unaging, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to sickness, having known the peril in sickness, seeks the unailing, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to death, having known the peril in death, seeks the deathless, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna; being himself subject to defilement, having known the peril in defilement, seeks the undefiled, supreme security from bondage, Nibbāna. These, monks, are the four noble searches.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.255
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: - What oppresses the world? What envelops the world? What arrow pierces the world? With what is it always smeared? - Death oppresses the world,…
item.description:
- What oppresses the world?
What envelops the world?
What arrow pierces the world?
With what is it always smeared?
- Death oppresses the world,
Aging envelops the world,
The arrow of craving pierces the world,
With sensual desires it is always smeared.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.66
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, a woman, attending to her own female faculties, female deportment, female attire, female nature, female desires, female voice, female adornment — becomes lustful and…
item.description:
“Monks, a woman, attending to her own female faculties, female deportment, female attire, female nature, female desires, female voice, female adornment — becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, she attends to external male faculties, male deportment, male attire, male nature, male desires, male voice, male adornment, and becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, she desires external bonding. With that bonding as condition, pleasure and joy arise, and she desires that pleasure and joy. Monks, through delighting in their own femininity, beings become bonded to men. Thus, monks, a woman does not escape her own femininity.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.51
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And Nigrodha, there are unwholesome states that have not been abandoned, that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, bringing suffering, resulting in pain, leading to…
item.description:
“And Nigrodha, there are unwholesome states that have not been abandoned, that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, bringing suffering, resulting in pain, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Those states I teach for the purpose of abandoning them. If you practice in accordance with the teaching, then those defiling states will be abandoned, the pure states will increase, and you will personally know, realize, and attain to abiding here and now with perfect and complete wisdom.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 25 – Udumbarikasutta

item.title: Elder Hatthārohaputta: “This mind formerly wandered Wherever it wished, as it liked, as it pleased. Now I will restrain it thoroughly With wise reflection, As…
item.description:
Elder Hatthārohaputta:
“This mind formerly wandered
Wherever it wished, as it liked, as it pleased.
Now I will restrain it thoroughly
With wise reflection,
As a driver with a hook
Restrains a rutting elephant.”

From: Theragāthā 1.77
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome, monks,…
item.description:
“Monks, if anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome, monks, is just the five hindrances. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill-will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, the hindrance of doubt. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome is just the five hindrances. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the wholesome,’ monks, he would speak rightly of the four foundations of mindfulness. The entire heap of the wholesome, monks, is just the four foundations of mindfulness. What four? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and sorrow in the world; dwells contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and sorrow in the world. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the wholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the four foundations of mindfulness. The entire heap of the wholesome is just the four foundations of mindfulness.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 47.5
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Sensual desire, monks, is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. Ill-will, monks … sloth and torpor … restlessness and…
item.description:
“Sensual desire, monks, is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. Ill-will, monks … sloth and torpor … restlessness and remorse … doubt is an obscuration, a hindrance, a covering of the mind, debilitating to wisdom. These, monks, are the five obscurations, hindrances, coverings of the mind, debilitating to wisdom.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.51

item.title: Those who are intoxicated with states, Bewildered and confused, Led astray into wrong courses, Wandering amidst various views — They sleep on and on, They…
item.description:
Those who are intoxicated with states,
Bewildered and confused,
Led astray into wrong courses,
Wandering amidst various views —
They sleep on and on,
They do not wake up.
Now indeed the time has come
For them to awaken.

(The Blessed One):
Those who are not intoxicated with states,
Not bewildered or confused,
Not led astray into wrong courses,
Wandering amidst various views —
They have attained perfect enlightenment,
They have fully understood.
On the uneven path,
They walk evenly.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.8
